rule_meaning: Nothing contradicts the idea strongly enough to stop or pivot, but there is not enough established, relevant evidence to go on.

missing_evidence: Independent sources supporting the problem statement: 0 of 2 needed (0 established findings, 0 people describing it in their own words).
1 needs-review and 1 partial findings do not count. A person may check them against their quotes; they never count automatically.
2 findings were off-topic for this brief and were not counted.
Demand and willingness to pay (A6): Desk research cannot establish demand or willingness to pay; only experiments with target customers can.
Validation conditions: none set. Set pass marks before running any experiment.

experiments.name: Ask 10 remote workers about Slack thread
experiments.support_if: At least 5 say they miss important messages in long Slack threads
experiments.weaken_if: All say they don't miss messages or they use other tools to catch up

experiments.name: Ask 5 remote engineers about Slack
experiments.support_if: At least 3 say they miss messages in Slack threads
experiments.weaken_if: All say they don't miss messages or they use other tools

experiments.name: Problem interviews
experiments.method: Talk to people who match 'remote engineers and product managers on distributed teams' about the last time they dealt with this problem. Ask what happened and what they did; do not pitch the idea.
experiments.support_if: Most interviewees describe a recent, specific occurrence without being prompted. Write down the pass mark before you start, as a validation condition in the brief.
experiments.weaken_if: Most cannot recall a recent occurrence, or say it is minor or already solved.

experiments.name: Wider desk research
experiments.method: Re-run the investigation with public pages where target customers discuss the problem (forums, communities, reviews of existing tools), added as source URLs in the brief.
experiments.support_if: Several different people describe the problem in their own words; these become established, relevant findings.
experiments.weaken_if: Relevant sources exist but people describe the problem as rare, minor or solved.

counterfactual.reconsidered_by: phase1_evidence_gate (run again with the new evidence)
counterfactual.no_guarantee: New evidence can strengthen or weaken the case. Running these experiments does not guarantee a GO decision, customers or income.
